messages.subject: Re: Reading multiple lines or just the whole chunk(64M split) in the mapper function.
parts:
On Friday, November 23, 2012 2:16:30 PM UTC+1, cyang05 wrote:
In Hadoop, the mapper functions are mostly line oriented (The framework feed the mapper line by line.). Well, if you write your code in java, you can write your own recordreader to process multiple lines a time(Of course, very hard, boundary-problem).  I just wonder could we write R code(The mapper) to read multiple lines a time or even the whole file split ( Say a 64M file split) a time? If so, then: 
          map = function(k, v) { v <- factor(v); table(v) } or { table(factor(v)) } #parallel-factoring -> extracting level counts -> reducer

I just wonder chunk oriented mapper could be more efficient than line oriented mapper in some cases( Well, we should take the amount of memory available into account, try to control the mapper to not to exceed the resource of datanode while running.).

Well, just a suggestion.

Thanks, this suggestion was implemented in 1.3 and is the default from 2.0 

Another doubt: I think sampling is meant to avoid "big data", right? Does anyone compare the results from samples with it from using the whole data? Is there any significant difference between using sample and using whole data? 

This question seems better suited for a statistics forum, here we discuss RHadoop.


Antonio
 

Thanks, I'm just a beginner. Maybe these are just silly questions.
